clue.text: Matter for rumination in the church luminant in Scotland

parts.note: kirk is the Scots word for a church
cud is what a cow chews over when ruminating
something luminant gives off light, so it is bright

explanation.surface: A sermon topic preached in a well-lit Scottish church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matter for rumination' reads as food for thought, but it is literally the cud a cow chews. KIRKCUDBRIGHT is a small town in south-west Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names a town in Galloway, so it is a place found in Scotland.

clue.text: What to do with football boots first and last?

definitions.text: What to do with football boots first and last?

parts.words: What to do with football boots first and last?
parts.note: the phrase that starts a football match is also what a player does to his boots when the game is over

explanation.definitionFit: A football match starts with the opening kick, and a player ends the day by booting his boots off his feet.

clue.text: Drove badly, was all over the place

indicators.note: done badly, the letters of the driving word are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: An erratic motorist swerved everywhere on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges DROVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rove is to wander widely, so someone who roved went all about.

clue.text: Weed prevalent on Newmarket Heath

parts.note: Newmarket Heath is horse-racing country, so young horses' hooves are everywhere there, naming a yellow-flowered weed

explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket Heath, in Suffolk, is the home of English horse racing and training.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant is a common yellow wild flower, and young male horses' feet are thick on the gallops of a racing town.

clue.text: Swift to the forest!

definitions.meaning: Jonathan Swift, author of Gulliver's Travels
the Forest of ... is an ancient woodland in Gloucestershire

explanation.definitionFit: The satirist held the church title of head of a cathedral chapter, and the same word names a Gloucestershire woodland.

clue.text: That corny domestic plot

parts.note: rye is a cereal crop, so something corny is to do with grain
domestic matters are those of the house

explanation.surface: A trite little scheme hatched at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rye House Plot of 1683 aimed to kill Charles II near Rye House in Hertfordshire; the answer alone stands for the conspiracy.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1683 conspiracy against the king is known by the name of the Hertfordshire mansion where it was to happen.

clue.text: Am in a pull-up, that's all

indicators.note: the word am is placed inside the turned-round pull
in a down clue, up means the word for pull is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to tug is to pull
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gymnast declares that one chin-up is their limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TUG into GUT, and 'in' puts AM inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole range of something, from one end to the other, is everything, the lot.

clue.text: Abram's docked bull under canvas is far from placid

indicators.note: being under canvas means being inside a tent, so the other pieces go within it

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas
Ur of the Chaldees was Abram's home city in Genesis

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the last letter of bull is removed

explanation.surface: A patriarch's bull, its tail cut, is restless while camping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' cuts BULL to BUL; UR and BUL then go 'under' canvas, inside TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wild and agitated is the opposite of calm and placid.

clue.text: Article Miss Linton has come about in place of Tennyson's rejected cycle

indicators.note: Cathy has come around the article, enclosing it

parts.note: Cathy Linton is the daughter of Catherine in Wuthering Heights
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A story about a young woman from a novel replaces a Tennyson poem.
explanation.walkthrough: In Locksley Hall Tennyson wrote 'Better fifty years of Europe than a cycle of Cathay', rejecting that cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet preferred fifty European years to a cycle of old China, the land named in that line.

clue.text: One of the Ridings staged

parts.note: a riding is a procession of horsemen, and Noel Coward's play of that name was staged in 1931; the Ridings also suggests Yorkshire's old divisions

explanation.walkthrough: The Ridings were the three old divisions of Yorkshire, which is the false trail here.
explanation.definitionFit: A procession on horseback is a riding, and the word is also the title of a Coward stage play.

clue.text: She's back with highest grade butter

indicators.note: back means the pieces that follow are written in reverse order

parts.note: A1 is the top rating, written AI
a ram butts, so it is a butter

explanation.surface: A woman returns with the finest dairy spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses AIRAM; 'butter' is one who butts, not the spread.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name stands for any female person.

clue.text: Sound antique ceramic? So-so

indicators.note: sound means the phrase is spoken, and its sound is spelt as the answer

parts.note: an old dish is an antique piece of pottery

explanation.surface: Asking whether a vintage pot is intact gets a lukewarm reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'undamaged', but it signals what is heard: OLD DISH said quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat aged means only moderately old, a middling or so-so age.

clue.text: Run on the drink in Ireland

indicators.note: on means the run comes after the drink in an across clue

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
to rush is to run

explanation.surface: A dash to the bar somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: PORTRUSH is a seaside resort in County Antrim, Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a resort town on the north Antrim coast, a place on the island of Ireland.

clue.text: Transformed to wolf, he was the man for Martha

definitions.text: he was the man for Martha

indicators.note: transformed means the letters of to wolf take a new shape

explanation.surface: A werewolf tale where a man changes and courts a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transformed' rearranges TO WOLF. Friedrich von Flotow composed the opera Martha (1847).
explanation.definitionFit: The German composer wrote the opera Martha, so he was its creator.

clue.text: Vernally bored children

parts.note: being off something means being tired of it
vernal means of the spring season

explanation.surface: Kids who grow weary each spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vernally bored' reads as 'off spring': fed up with the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Children are the issue or progeny of their parents.

clue.text: Stringed instrument, but the piano is mute

definitions.text: Stringed instrument, but the piano is mute

parts.words: Stringed instrument, but the piano is mute
parts.note: piano is P in music, and this old plucked instrument's name begins with a silent P

explanation.definitionFit: The medieval plucked zither-like instrument is spelt with an opening P that is never pronounced.

clue.text: Patronized by Lucasta for a gift, to please her man?

definitions.text: Patronized by Lucasta for a gift, to please her man?

parts.words: Patronized by Lucasta for a gift, to please her man?
parts.note: Lucasta was the beloved of the poet Richard Lovelace, so a gift that pleases her man must be one he would love: lace

explanation.definitionFit: A craftswoman who produces lace would serve Lucasta, whose poet admirer was named Lovelace.

clue.text: Serious in combinations worn by disorientated gal in the harem

indicators.note: worn by means one piece is wrapped round the other like clothing

parts.note: serio- is the combining form of serious, as in serio-comic

indicators.note: disorientated means the letters of gal are turned about

explanation.surface: A solemn girl in underwear loses her bearings in a sultan's quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorientated' turns GAL into AGL, which sits inside SERIO. 'Combinations' looks like underwear but means word combinations.
explanation.definitionFit: The women's quarters of an Ottoman palace were called by this name.

clue.text: Made shipshape again

parts.note: a ship back in the dock is repaired and fitted out once more

explanation.definitionFit: A ship that is overhauled and re-equipped is put back in good order.

clue.text: Jackin' up a plum job

parts.note: jacking up is ..., said with a dropped g, and in plum pudding the plums are dried grapes

explanation.definitionFit: Raising with the final g dropped sounds like the dried grape that plays the plum in a plum pudding.

clue.text: Bill to quote returning the acid

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: returning means the word for quote is written backwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: A shop sends back an invoice quoting a sour price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns CITE into ETIC, placed after AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic describes the sour, vinegary quality of acid.

clue.text: Hot basket wanting mustard too ?

parts.note: an iron fire basket whose name starts with the salad leaf that usually goes with mustard

explanation.definitionFit: The iron basket holding burning fuel as a beacon begins with the leaf of mustard-and-cress.

clue.text: Pint-size beard ?.

definitions.meaning: the British pint is a unit of the old system of measures named after the empire
a small pointed tuft on the chin, as worn by Napoleon III

explanation.definitionFit: The empire's system of measures defines the British pint, and a pointed chin tuft takes the same name.

clue.text: Run me in, in Cowes? Hear, Hear!

definitions.text: Run me in, in Cowes? Hear, Hear!

parts.words: Run me in, in Cowes? Hear, Hear!
parts.note: Cowes is heard as cows, and the stomach that a cow's food runs into first sounds like a run me

explanation.walkthrough: Cowes is a sailing town on the Isle of Wight; the clue asks it to be heard as 'cows'.
explanation.definitionFit: The first stomach of a cow, where swallowed food goes in, is called by this name.

clue.text: Points about the legend of a man of the mountains.

indicators.note: about means the points go around the legend

parts.note: S and E are compass points
a myth is a legend

explanation.surface: Compass directions around a mountain folk tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank Smythe was a noted British mountaineer of the 1930s Everest expeditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Smythe was a celebrated climber of the Himalaya.

clue.text: Sing to attract the fish, little man

definitions.meaning: to sing a song merrily in parts
to fish by trailing a baited line behind a boat

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to sing heartily, to fish with a trailed line, and a goblin of Norse legend.

clue.text: With a yen for a sixpence

parts.note: six in Roman numerals is VI, and d is the old British penny

explanation.surface: Keen on a small silver coin.
explanation.walkthrough: D stood for a penny in pre-decimal British money, so VI D is sixpence. 'yen' looks like money but means longing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being eager and keen means longing for something.

clue.text: City that stopped work on high-rise blocks?

definitions.text: City that stopped work on high-rise blocks?

parts.words: City that stopped work on high-rise blocks?
parts.note: Marlowe wrote of the topless towers of Troy, as if the builders stopped before the tops

explanation.definitionFit: Troy's other name appears in Marlowe's line about its topless towers, towers left unfinished.

clue.text: Bows making nil headway through the water?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring
a ship's speed is measured in knots

explanation.surface: A ship's prow making no progress at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bows' looks like the front of a ship, but means ribbon bows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental ribbons tied as tokens of affection are decorative bows.

clue.text: More than a double-barrelled attempt at killing

definitions.text: More than a double-barrelled attempt at killing

parts.words: More than a double-barrelled attempt at killing
parts.note: the 1605 scheme to blow up king and Parliament used barrels of explosive, far more than a double-barrelled gun

explanation.walkthrough: Guy Fawkes and fellow conspirators stored 36 barrels under the House of Lords in 1605.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1605 conspiracy to blow up Parliament used dozens of barrels of explosive, more than two.
